title: Group Fitness Class Passes: the per-credit reference value recorded when a pack is archived
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Group Fitness Class Passes product line. It states how the per-credit dollar reference value recorded when an exhausted or expired pack is archived is calculated, and how a corporate wellness enrollment affects it.

## Basis
The per-credit reference value is the tier's purchase price divided by the number of credits the tier includes. For the Unlimited Monthly Classes tier, which has no fixed per-credit value because it grants unlimited use rather than a finite credit count, this reference value is zero. Where the archiving member holds an active corporate wellness enrollment at the time of archival, the per-credit reference value is further discounted by the lesser of the employer's own discount rate under that enrollment and the tier's own corporate wellness discount rate; the two rates are compared and only the lower one is applied, never both together. A member without an active corporate wellness enrollment at that time has the undiscounted reference value recorded. The value recorded, whichever way it was arrived at, is rounded to two decimal places.

## Input-judgement-output
1. Is the pack's tier Unlimited Monthly Classes? If yes, the per-credit reference value is zero and no corporate discount changes that outcome.
2. If no, divide the tier's purchase price by the tier's included credit count to obtain the undiscounted per-credit reference value.
3. Is the archiving member's corporate wellness enrollment active at the moment of archival? If no, record the undiscounted value from step 2. If yes, apply the lesser of the employer's rate and the tier's own corporate wellness discount rate to that value, then round to two decimal places.

## Hypothetical worked example (illustration only)
Suppose, purely for illustration, a tier's purchase price were $200.00 for 10 included credits (an undiscounted per-credit value of $20.00), the tier's own corporate wellness discount rate were 7 percent, and the archiving member's employer offered 4 percent. The lower rate, 4 percent, applies to the $20.00 figure, and the outcome is rounded to two decimal places. Had no active enrollment existed, $20.00 would be recorded unchanged.

## Points of judgement
- This reference value is informational only; recording it does not itself credit or debit any cash account.
- Whether the enrollment is active is judged at the moment of archival, not at the moment the pack originally became exhausted or expired.
